records.source: אֵ֠לֶּה הַֽחֻקִּ֣ים וְהַמִּשְׁפָּטִים֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּשְׁמְר֣וּן לַעֲשׂוֹת֒ בָּאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁר֩ נָתַ֨ן יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֧י אֲבֹתֶ֛יךָ לְךָ֖ לְרִשְׁתָּ֑הּ כָּל־הַיָּמִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־אַתֶּ֥ם חַיִּ֖ים עַל־הָאֲדָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: These [are] the statutes and the judgments which you will take care to do in the land which has given Yahweh [the] God of your fathers to you to possess it, all the days which you [are] living on the ground.
pieces: These are the statutes and rulings you must be careful to keep in the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your ancestors, has given you to possess, for as long as you live on its soil.

L.1: These [are] the statutes and the judgments that you shall be careful to do in the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your fathers, has given you to take possession of it, all the days that you live on the ground.

R.1: Here are the laws and rules you must be careful to obey in the land. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your ancestors, has given it to you to take as your own. Obey them for as long as you live there.

decisions.choice: the statutes and the judgments: the whole body of law that follows
decisions.reason: The pair names the laws Moses promised to teach (4:1, 5:1, 6:1). This verse is the heading of the long section of laws that runs to 26:19, still inside the speech Moses began at 5:1. It closes with the same pair (26:16).

decisions.choice: has given: the gift is certain, though the land is not yet entered
decisions.reason: The verb is in the completed form even though Israel is still east of the Jordan (verse 10). The land is spoken of as already given because God's promise settles it.

decisions.choice: on the ground: on the soil of the land, for as long as you live
decisions.reason: The word is the ground or soil, the farmed earth. "All the days you live on the ground" means for the whole of life in the land (4:10; 31:13); the laws are for life in the land, not only for the journey.

decisions.choice: statutes and judgments / statutes and rulings / laws and rules
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this pair in these books: Literal keeps "judgments", Balanced says "rulings", Readable "laws and rules".

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: The "fathers" are Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and the generations after them. Balanced and Readable say "ancestors"; Literal keeps "fathers".

records.heading: The place {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will choose

records.source: אַבֵּ֣ד תְּ֠אַבְּדוּן אֶֽת־כָּל־הַמְּקֹמ֞וֹת אֲשֶׁ֧ר עָֽבְדוּ־שָׁ֣ם הַגּוֹיִ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתֶּ֛ם יֹרְשִׁ֥ים אֹתָ֖ם אֶת־אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֑ם עַל־הֶהָרִ֤ים הָֽרָמִים֙ וְעַל־הַגְּבָע֔וֹת וְתַ֖חַת כָּל־עֵ֥ץ רַעֲנָן׃
records.gloss: Destroying you shall destroy all the places where served there the nations whom you [are] dispossessing them their gods, on the mountains the high and on the hills and under every tree green.
pieces: You must completely destroy all the places where the nations you are driving out worshiped their gods, on the high mountains, on the hills, and under every leafy tree.

L.2: You shall utterly destroy all the places where the nations whom you are dispossessing served their gods, on the high mountains and on the hills and under every green tree.

R.2: The nations you are driving out worshiped their gods in many places: on high mountains, on hills, and under every green tree. You must destroy all those places completely.

decisions.choice: destroying you shall destroy: destroy completely
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. It is the ordinary verb "destroy", used of the places of worship and their objects, not the word for devoting to destruction used of the nations themselves (7:2).

decisions.choice: high mountains, hills, green trees: the open-air shrines of the land
decisions.reason: Hilltops and large leafy trees were favored places for worship in Canaan. The prophets and the histories name them again and again as places of false worship (1 Kings 14:23; 2 Kings 17:10; Jeremiah 2:20; Hosea 4:13).

decisions.choice: served: worshiped
decisions.reason: To "serve" a god is to worship it with offerings and rites. The same verb is used of serving the LORD (10:12).

decisions.choice: worshiped / driving out
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "worshiped" for "served", which is its sense here. The verb for taking the nations' place is "dispossess" at Literal and "drive out" at Balanced and Readable, as settled for Deuteronomy.

records.source: וְנִתַּצְתֶּ֣ם אֶת־מִזְבּחֹתָ֗םוְשִׁבַּרְתֶּם֙ אֶת־מַצֵּ֣בֹתָ֔ם וַאֲשֵֽׁרֵיהֶם֙ תִּשְׂרְפ֣וּן בָּאֵ֔שׁ וּפְסִילֵ֥י אֱלֹֽהֵיהֶ֖ם תְּגַדֵּע֑וּן וְאִבַּדְתֶּ֣ם אֶת־שְׁמָ֔ם מִן־הַמָּק֖וֹם הַהֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And you will pull down their altars, and you will shatter their pillars, and their Asherah poles you will burn with fire, and [the] carved images of their gods you will cut down, and you will destroy their name from the place the that.
pieces: Tear down their altars, smash their sacred stones, burn their Asherah poles, cut down the carved images of their gods, and wipe out their name from that place.

L.3: And you shall tear down their altars and smash their pillars, and their Asherah poles you shall burn with fire, and the carved images of their gods you shall cut down, and you shall destroy their name from that place.

R.3: Tear down their altars. Smash their stone pillars. Burn the poles used to worship the goddess Asherah. Cut down the statues of their gods. Wipe out the names of those gods from every such place.

decisions.choice: altars, pillars, Asherah poles: the same command as 7:5
decisions.reason: The list repeats 7:5 and Exodus 34:13 almost word for word, and adds the carved images. Here it serves a new point: these places must go so that Israel will worship only at the place God chooses (verses 4-5).

decisions.choice: pillars: standing stones set up as sacred objects
decisions.reason: A standing stone marked a holy place or stood for a god. Israel was forbidden to set them up (16:22; Leviticus 26:1), though earlier Jacob had set one up as a memorial (Genesis 28:18).

decisions.choice: Asherah poles: wooden poles or trees for the goddess Asherah
decisions.reason: Asherah was a Canaanite goddess. Her symbol was a wooden pole or a tree planted beside an altar (16:21), which is why it is burned and cut down.

decisions.choice: destroy their name: remove every trace of the gods' worship
decisions.reason: "Their name" is the name of the nations' gods. Calling on a god's name was the heart of worship there; destroying the name means that no one will call on those gods at that place again. Verse 5 sets against this the place where the LORD puts his own name.

decisions.choice: the poles used to worship the goddess Asherah; the names of those gods
decisions.reason: Readable explains Asherah, as settled for these books, and says whose name is meant.

records.source: לֹֽא־תַעֲשׂ֣וּן כֵּ֔ן לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Not you shall do so to Yahweh your God.
pieces: You must not worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God in that way.

L.4: You shall not do so to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

R.4: Do not worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God the way they worship their gods.

decisions.choice: do so: worship the LORD as the nations worshiped their gods, at many places of your own choosing
alternatives: do not destroy the LORD's altars or name as you destroy theirs
decisions.reason: "So" points back to verse 2: the nations worshiped wherever they chose, on any hill or under any tree. Verse 5 gives the contrast: Israel is to come to the one place God chooses. Another reading takes "so" with verse 3: do not destroy what bears the LORD's name as you destroy theirs. The flow into verse 5 favors the first.

decisions.choice: worship ... in that way
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "do so" means here: the way of worship just described. Literal keeps "do so".

records.source: כִּ֠י אִֽם־אֶל־הַמָּק֞וֹם אֲשֶׁר־יִבְחַ֨ר יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶם֙ מִכָּל־שִׁבְטֵיכֶ֔ם לָשׂ֥וּם אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ שָׁ֑ם לְשִׁכְנ֥וֹ תִדְרְשׁ֖וּ וּבָ֥אתָ שָֽׁמָּה׃
records.gloss: But rather to the place which will choose Yahweh your God from all your tribes to put his name there, for his dwelling you shall seek, and you will come there.
pieces: Instead, you must seek the place that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will choose out of all your tribes to put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name there as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} dwelling, and go there.

L.5: But the place that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will choose out of all your tribes to put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name there, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} dwelling, you shall seek, and there you shall come.

R.5: Instead, go to the one place that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will choose from among all your tribes. He will put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name there and make it {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} home. Go there to worship {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: the place he will choose: one place of worship, chosen by God and not by Israel
decisions.reason: The phrase returns through chapters 12-26 (verses 11, 14, 18, 21, 26; 14:23; 16:2). The place is not named. Later it was Shiloh for a time (Joshua 18:1; Jeremiah 7:12) and then Jerusalem (1 Kings 8:29; 2 Kings 21:4). Verse 14 says "in one of your tribes".

decisions.choice: to put his name there: to mark the place as his own and as where he meets his people
decisions.reason: God's name stands for God himself as he is known and called on. Putting his name on a place claims it as his and makes it the place where he is present to hear his people, while he is not confined to it (Exodus 20:24; 1 Kings 8:27-29).

decisions.choice: his dwelling: a noun taken with "you shall seek", following the Hebrew accents
alternatives: to put his name there, to make it dwell; you shall seek [it]
decisions.reason: The word can be read as a noun, "his dwelling", or as a verb, "to make it dwell", which would join it to "to put his name there" (as verse 11 says "to make his name dwell there"). The accents end the first clause after "there" and join "his dwelling" to "you shall seek". Either way the place is where God's name lives among his people.

decisions.choice: seek: go there to worship
decisions.reason: To seek a place or a god here means to go to it to worship and to ask for help (verse 30 uses the same verb of asking about the nations' gods). It is not a search for a hidden place: God will make the place known.

decisions.choice: the one place ... Go there to worship him
decisions.reason: Readable adds "one" from verse 14 and says why Israel is to go there, which "seek" implies.

records.source: וַהֲבֵאתֶ֣ם שָׁ֗מָּה עֹלֹֽתֵיכֶם֙ וְזִבְחֵיכֶ֔ם וְאֵת֙ מַעְשְׂרֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם וְאֵ֖ת תְּרוּמַ֣ת יֶדְכֶ֑ם וְנִדְרֵיכֶם֙ וְנִדְבֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם וּבְכֹרֹ֥ת בְּקַרְכֶ֖ם וְצֹאנְכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And you shall bring there your burnt offerings and your sacrifices and your tithes and [the] contribution of your hand, and your vows and your freewill offerings and [the] firstborn of your herd and your flock.
pieces: Bring there your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and the gifts you set apart, your vow offerings and your freewill offerings, and the firstborn of your herds and flocks.

L.6: And there you shall bring your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, and your tithes and the contribution of your hand, and your vow offerings and your freewill offerings, and the firstborn of your herd and of your flock.

R.6: Bring all your offerings there: your burnt offerings and other sacrifices, the tenth of your crops, your special gifts, the gifts you promised to give, the gifts you choose to give, and the firstborn of your cattle, sheep and goats.

decisions.choice: burnt offerings and sacrifices: offerings burned whole, and offerings shared in a meal
decisions.reason: A burnt offering was burned entirely on the altar (Leviticus 1). A "sacrifice" here is an animal slaughtered for a meal: part went on the altar and the worshipers ate the rest, like the peace offering (Leviticus 3; 7:11-18). This is why verse 7 says "you shall eat there".

decisions.choice: tithes: a tenth of the year's produce
decisions.reason: A tenth of grain, wine and oil was set apart each year (14:22-29). Deuteronomy has it eaten at the chosen place by the family, with the Levite (verses 17-18).

decisions.choice: the contribution of your hand: a gift taken off and set apart for God
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "lift" or "take off": a portion lifted out from what one has and given to the sanctuary (Exodus 25:2; Numbers 18:24). "Of your hand" means what you yourself give.

decisions.choice: vow offerings and freewill offerings: gifts once promised, and gifts given of one's own accord
decisions.reason: A vow offering paid a promise made to God, often when asking his help; a freewill offering was given with no promise or obligation (Leviticus 7:16; 22:18-23).

decisions.choice: the gifts you set apart; the tenth of your crops; the gifts you promised / choose to give
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the "contribution of your hand" is. Readable explains each offering in plain words, and says "cattle, sheep and goats", since a flock was of both.

records.source: וַאֲכַלְתֶּם־שָׁ֗ם לִפְנֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם וּשְׂמַחְתֶּ֗ם בְּכֹל֙ מִשְׁלַ֣ח יֶדְכֶ֔ם אַתֶּ֖ם וּבָתֵּיכֶ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר בֵּֽרַכְךָ֖ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And you shall eat there before Yahweh your God, and you shall rejoice in all [the] undertaking of your hand, you and your households, which has blessed you Yahweh your God.
pieces: There you and your households are to eat in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and rejoice in all that you have set your hand to, all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has blessed you with.

L.7: And you shall eat there before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and you shall rejoice in all the undertaking of your hand, you and your households, in which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has blessed you.

R.7: There, in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, you and your families will eat and be glad for everything you have worked for. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has blessed you with it all.

decisions.choice: eat there before the LORD: a joyful meal at the sanctuary
decisions.reason: The worshipers ate their share of the sacrifices, tithes and firstborn at the chosen place, as a feast in God's presence (14:23-26; 16:11). "Before the LORD" means at the place where he is present.

decisions.choice: the undertaking of your hand: whatever you work at, and what it yields
decisions.reason: "Sending out the hand" is an idiom for one's work and its results (15:10; 23:21; 28:8). Israel rejoices in the harvest and herds God has made its work produce.

decisions.choice: you (plural) and you (singular): the people as a whole and each one of them
decisions.reason: The chapter moves between "you" plural and "you" singular, here within one verse. Moses speaks both to all Israel and to each Israelite as one; the meaning does not change.

decisions.choice: you and your households are to eat
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring "you and your households" forward to the start, so it is clear who eats and rejoices. "Families" at Readable is the plain word for the households.

records.source: לֹ֣א תַעֲשׂ֔וּן כְּ֠כֹל אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֲנַ֧חְנוּ עֹשִׂ֛ים פֹּ֖ה הַיּ֑וֹם אִ֖ישׁ כָּל־הַיָּשָׁ֥ר בְּעֵינָֽיו׃
records.gloss: Not you shall do according to all that we [are] doing here the day, each man all the right in his eyes,
pieces: You must not do as we are doing here today, everyone doing whatever seems right to them,

L.8: You shall not do according to all that we are doing here today, each {{gender:one|man}} [doing] whatever [is] right in {{gender:their|his}} own eyes,

R.8: Do not keep doing what we are doing here today. Now everyone does whatever they think is right.

decisions.choice: what we are doing here today: the way worship is done now, on the plains of Moab
decisions.reason: Moses includes himself. On the journey there was no settled place and no rest (verse 9), so practice was not yet ordered as it will be. The verse does not say exactly what was irregular; it may be offerings made in many places, or worship left to each person's choice.

decisions.choice: right in his own eyes: what each one thinks is right
decisions.reason: The phrase sets a person's own judgment against what God has commanded; verses 25 and 28 speak of doing what is right "in the eyes of the LORD". Judges uses it of a time with no order (Judges 17:6; 21:25).

decisions.choice: each man: each person, man or woman
decisions.reason: The word is "man", used in the sense "each one".

decisions.choice: each {{gender:one|man}} (Literal); everyone (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the traditional "man" as the setting's alternative. Balanced and Readable say "everyone", which needs no setting.

records.source: כִּ֥י לֹא־בָּאתֶ֖ם עַד־עָ֑תָּה אֶל־הַמְּנוּחָה֙ וְאֶל־הַֽנַּחֲלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: for not you have come until now to the resting place and to the inheritance which Yahweh your God [is] giving to you.
pieces: because you have not yet reached the place of rest, the inheritance that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you.

L.9: for you have not yet come to the resting place and to the inheritance that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you.

R.9: That is because you have not yet come to the land of rest. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving it to you to keep as your own.

decisions.choice: the resting place: a settled home, free from wandering and from enemies
decisions.reason: The word means rest or a place of rest. Here it is the land where Israel will settle, with its enemies held off (verse 10; 1 Kings 8:56). Psalm 95:11 recalls it: "they shall not enter my rest".

decisions.choice: the inheritance: the land as a lasting family possession, given by God
decisions.reason: An inheritance is property that stays in a family from one generation to the next. Israel's land is called this because God gives it and it is to remain theirs (4:21; 15:4).

decisions.choice: the place of rest, the inheritance (Balanced); the land of rest ... to keep as your own (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable take the two nouns as two names for one land, which the verse's "which" implies. Readable explains "inheritance" in plain words.

records.source: וַעֲבַרְתֶּם֮ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּן֒ וִֽישַׁבְתֶּ֣ם בָּאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֖ם מַנְחִ֣יל אֶתְכֶ֑ם וְהֵנִ֨יחַ לָכֶ֧ם מִכָּל־אֹיְבֵיכֶ֛ם מִסָּבִ֖יב וִֽישַׁבְתֶּם־בֶּֽטַח׃
records.gloss: And you will cross the Jordan and you will live in the land which Yahweh your God [is] causing to inherit you, and he will give rest to you from all your enemies from around, and you will live [in] security,
pieces: But you will cross the Jordan and settle in the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you as an inheritance. He will give you rest from all the enemies around you, and you will live in safety,

L.10: But you will cross the Jordan and live in the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you to inherit, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give you rest from all your enemies around [you], and you will live in security,

R.10: But you will cross the Jordan River and live in the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you. He will keep you safe from all the enemies around you, and you will live without fear.

decisions.choice: and you will cross: the time to come, which sets the scene for verse 11
decisions.reason: The verbs speak of the future, after the crossing. Verse 11 says what will follow once Israel lives in the land in safety: then the place God chooses will be the only place for offerings.

decisions.choice: give rest from enemies; live in security: peace on every side
decisions.reason: God's giving of "rest" means an end to war with the neighboring peoples (25:19; Joshua 21:44; 2 Samuel 7:1). "In security" means without danger or fear. The same promise is made in Leviticus 25:18-19.

decisions.choice: the Jordan River
decisions.reason: Readable adds "River" so the name is clear.

records.source: וְהָיָ֣ה הַמָּק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁר־יִבְחַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֥ם בּוֹ֙ לְשַׁכֵּ֤ן שְׁמוֹ֙ שָׁ֔ם שָׁ֣מָּה תָבִ֔יאוּ אֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י מְצַוֶּ֣ה אֶתְכֶ֑ם עוֹלֹתֵיכֶ֣ם וְזִבְחֵיכֶ֗ם מַעְשְׂרֹֽתֵיכֶם֙ וּתְרֻמַ֣ת יֶדְכֶ֔ם וְכֹל֙ מִבְחַ֣ר נִדְרֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּדְּר֖וּ לַֽיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: and it will be: the place which will choose Yahweh your God in it to make dwell his name there, there you shall bring all that I [am] commanding you: your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and [the] contribution of your hand, and all [the] choice of your vows which you will vow to Yahweh.
pieces: then you are to bring everything I am commanding you to the place that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will choose as a dwelling for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name: your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and the gifts you set apart, and all the fine offerings you vow to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.11: then it shall be [that] to the place that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will choose to make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name dwell there, there you shall bring all that I am commanding you: your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and the contribution of your hand, and all the choicest of your vow offerings that you vow to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.11: Then you must bring everything I command you to the place that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will choose as the home for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name. Bring your burnt offerings and other sacrifices, the tenth of your crops, your special gifts, and the best things you promised to give {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: to make his name dwell there: to make the place the home of his name
decisions.reason: The verb "dwell" is the one from which the word for the tabernacle comes. As in verse 5, God's name living at the place means that he is present there for his people and claims the place as his own.

decisions.choice: I am commanding you: Moses speaks
decisions.reason: "I" is Moses, who passes on the commands God gave him (5:31). The same phrase recurs in verses 14, 21 and 28.

decisions.choice: all the choice of your vows: your vow offerings, which are to be the best
alternatives: the best of your vow offerings
decisions.reason: "Choice" means the best, the pick of the flock or harvest. The phrase may mean that vow offerings must be the finest one has, or simply call all vow offerings "choice" gifts. Either way nothing poor is to be vowed to God (Leviticus 22:18-21; Malachi 1:14).

decisions.choice: the list of offerings: as in verse 6
decisions.reason: The list repeats verse 6 in shorter form. See the notes there.

decisions.choice: you are to bring everything ... to the place
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names the place first and then says "there you shall bring". Balanced and Readable put the verb first, as English prefers. Literal keeps the Hebrew order.

records.source: וּשְׂמַחְתֶּ֗ם לִפְנֵי֮ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶם֒ אַתֶּ֗ם וּבְנֵיכֶם֙ וּבְנֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם וְעַבְדֵיכֶ֖ם וְאַמְהֹתֵיכֶ֑ם וְהַלֵּוִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּשַֽׁעֲרֵיכֶ֔ם כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין ל֛וֹ חֵ֥לֶק וְנַחֲלָ֖ה אִתְּכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And you shall rejoice before Yahweh your God, you and your sons and your daughters and your male slaves and your female slaves, and the Levite who [is] in your gates, for there is not to him portion and inheritance with you.
pieces: And you shall rejoice in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, you and your sons and daughters, your male and female servants, and the Levite who lives in your towns, since he has no share or inheritance among you.

L.12: And you shall rejoice before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, you and your sons and your daughters and your male slaves and your female slaves, and the Levite who [is] within your gates, for he has no portion or inheritance with you.

R.12: Celebrate there in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, together with your sons and daughters, your servants, and the Levites who live in your towns. The Levites have not been given land of their own as you have.

decisions.choice: male slaves and female slaves: men and women owned by the household
decisions.reason: These were people owned by a household, not hired workers. They share in the feast with the family, as in the Sabbath law (5:14) and the feasts (16:11, 14).

decisions.choice: within your gates: in your towns
decisions.reason: A town was entered through its gate, and "your gates" stands for the towns of Israel where people live.

decisions.choice: no portion or inheritance: the Levites received no tribal land
decisions.reason: The tribe of Levi was given towns to live in but no territory of its own; it lived from the offerings and tithes (10:9; 18:1-2; Numbers 18:20-24). That is why the Levite must be invited to the feast. "The Levite" stands for every Levite.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: Literal says "slaves"; Balanced and Readable say "servants", as the style guide sets for this word, while the meaning decision keeps the person's position.

decisions.choice: the Levites (plural)
decisions.reason: Readable says "the Levites", since the singular means the Levites as a group, and says "land of their own" for "portion or inheritance".

records.source: הִשָּׁ֣מֶר לְךָ֔ פֶּֽן־תַּעֲלֶ֖ה עֹלֹתֶ֑יךָ בְּכָל־מָק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּרְאֶֽה׃
records.gloss: Take heed to yourself lest you offer up your burnt offerings in every place which you see,
pieces: Be careful not to offer your burnt offerings at any place you happen to see,

L.13: Take care for yourself that you do not offer up your burnt offerings in every place that you see,

R.13: Be careful! Do not offer your burnt offerings just anywhere you like.

decisions.choice: every place that you see: any place that catches your eye
decisions.reason: The place would be chosen by what the worshiper sees and likes. Verse 14 sets against it the place the LORD "will choose".

decisions.choice: take care for yourself: a warning to each Israelite
decisions.reason: The verb is "guard yourself", a strong warning, and here the address is singular, to each person. It comes again in verses 19 and 30.

decisions.choice: just anywhere you like
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "any place you see": a place picked by one's own choice.

records.source: כִּ֣י אִם־בַּמָּק֞וֹם אֲשֶׁר־יִבְחַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ בְּאַחַ֣ד שְׁבָטֶ֔יךָ שָׁ֖ם תַּעֲלֶ֣ה עֹלֹתֶ֑יךָ וְשָׁ֣ם תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י מְצַוֶּֽךָּ׃
records.gloss: for only in the place which will choose Yahweh in one of your tribes, there you shall offer up your burnt offerings, and there you shall do all that I [am] commanding you.
pieces: but only at the place that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will choose in one of your tribes. There you are to offer your burnt offerings, and there you are to do everything I am commanding you.

L.14: but only in the place that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will choose in one of your tribes, there you shall offer up your burnt offerings, and there you shall do all that I am commanding you.

R.14: Offer them only at the place that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will choose in the land of one of your tribes. Do everything I command you there.

decisions.choice: in one of your tribes: one place, in the land of one tribe
decisions.reason: The phrase makes plain what verse 5 implied: not a place for each tribe but one for all of Israel, in the territory of one tribe. The tribe is not named.

decisions.choice: all that I am commanding you: all the offerings and rites set out here
decisions.reason: This means the sacrifices and gifts of verses 6 and 11 and the meals and celebration that go with them.

decisions.choice: the land of one of your tribes
decisions.reason: Readable adds "the land of": the place is in a tribe's territory.

records.source: רַק֩ בְּכָל־אַוַּ֨ת נַפְשְׁךָ֜ תִּזְבַּ֣ח׀וְאָכַלְתָּ֣ בָשָׂ֗ר כְּבִרְכַּ֨ת יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֶ֛יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָֽתַן־לְךָ֖ בְּכָל־שְׁעָרֶ֑יךָ הַטָּמֵ֤א וְהַטָּהוֹר֙ יֹאכְלֶ֔נּוּ כַּצְּבִ֖י וְכָאַיָּֽל׃
records.gloss: Only in all [the] desire of your soul you may slaughter and you may eat meat according to [the] blessing of Yahweh your God which he has given to you in all your gates; the unclean and the clean may eat it, as the gazelle and as the deer.
pieces: However, you may slaughter and eat meat in any of your towns whenever you wish, as much as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has blessed you with. Both those who are ritually unclean and those who are clean may eat it, as they would a gazelle or a deer.

L.15: Only, with all the desire of your soul you may slaughter and eat meat, according to the blessing of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given you, within all your gates; the unclean and the clean may eat it, as [they eat] the gazelle and the deer.

R.15: But you may kill animals and eat the meat in your own towns whenever you want, as much as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has blessed you with. Anyone may eat it, whether they are ritually clean or not, just as they would eat a gazelle or a deer.

decisions.choice: you may slaughter and eat meat in your towns: killing animals for food away from the altar
decisions.reason: Once worship is at one distant place, people may kill animals for ordinary meals at home, without offering them. This loosens the rule of the wilderness camp, where an animal killed for food was brought to the tent of meeting (Leviticus 17:3-5).

decisions.choice: with all the desire of your soul: whenever and as much as you want
decisions.reason: The "soul" here is the person with his appetite and wants (verse 20). The phrase gives free permission, limited only by what God has given.

decisions.choice: the unclean and the clean, as the gazelle and the deer: anyone may eat this meat
decisions.reason: Clean and unclean are states of fitness for worship, not moral states. Meat from an offering could be eaten only by someone ritually clean (Leviticus 7:19-21). Gazelle and deer were hunted game, never offered at the altar, so anyone could eat them; meat killed at home is treated in the same way.

decisions.choice: according to the blessing of the LORD: as far as his gifts allow
decisions.reason: How much meat a household could eat depended on the herds and flocks God had blessed it with. The phrase marks the meat as God's gift.

decisions.choice: ritually unclean / ritually clean
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "ritually" so that "unclean" is not read as dirty or sinful.

records.source: רַ֥ק הַדָּ֖ם לֹ֣א תֹאכֵ֑לוּ עַל־הָאָ֥רֶץ תִּשְׁפְּכֶ֖נּוּ כַּמָּֽיִם׃
records.gloss: Only the blood not you shall eat; on the ground you shall pour it like water.
pieces: But you must not eat the blood; pour it out on the ground like water.

L.16: Only the blood you shall not eat; on the ground you shall pour it out like water.

R.16: But do not eat the blood. Pour it out on the ground like water.

decisions.choice: not the blood: blood belongs to God, because it is the life
decisions.reason: The ban on eating blood goes back to Noah (Genesis 9:4) and is given its reason in Leviticus 17:10-14 and in verse 23 here: the life is in the blood. It holds for meat killed at home as much as for offerings.

decisions.choice: pour it out like water: a plain disposal, with no rite
decisions.reason: Blood from an offering was put on the altar (verse 27). Blood from an animal killed for food is simply poured on the ground, so that no one eats it. Leviticus 17:13 adds that the blood of game is covered with earth.

records.source: לֹֽא־תוּכַ֞ל לֶאֱכֹ֣ל בִּשְׁעָרֶ֗יךָ מַעְשַׂ֤ר דְּגָֽנְךָ֙ וְתִֽירֹשְׁךָ֣ וְיִצְהָרֶ֔ךָ וּבְכֹרֹ֥ת בְּקָרְךָ֖ וְצֹאנֶ֑ךָ וְכָל־נְדָרֶ֨יךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּדֹּ֔ר וְנִדְבֹתֶ֖יךָ וּתְרוּמַ֥ת יָדֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Not you are able to eat in your gates [the] tithe of your grain and your new wine and your oil, and [the] firstborn of your herd and your flock, and all your vows which you vow, and your freewill offerings and [the] contribution of your hand,
pieces: You may not eat in your own towns the tithe of your grain, new wine and oil, or the firstborn of your herds and flocks, or any of the offerings you vow, or your freewill offerings, or the gifts you set apart,

L.17: You may not eat within your gates the tithe of your grain or of your new wine or of your oil, or the firstborn of your herd or of your flock, or any of your vow offerings that you vow, or your freewill offerings, or the contribution of your hand,

R.17: But some things you must not eat in your own towns. These are the tenth of your grain, your new wine and your olive oil, the firstborn of your cattle, sheep and goats, the gifts you promised to give, the gifts you choose to give, and your other special gifts.

decisions.choice: you are not able to eat: you are not permitted to eat
decisions.reason: The verb "be able" with "not" here means what the law does not allow, not what is impossible (as in 16:5; 17:15).

decisions.choice: grain, new wine and oil: the three main crops of the land
decisions.reason: The three stand for the whole harvest (7:13; 11:14). "New wine" is the fresh juice of the grape harvest, and the oil is fresh olive oil.

decisions.choice: holy gifts set apart from ordinary meat
decisions.reason: Meat killed for a meal may be eaten anywhere (verse 15), but tithes, firstborn animals and vowed or freewill gifts belong to God and are eaten only at the chosen place (verse 18).

decisions.choice: olive oil
decisions.reason: Readable names the oil, which was pressed from olives.

records.source: כִּ֡י אִם־לִפְנֵי֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ תֹּאכְלֶ֗נּוּ בַּמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִבְחַ֜ר יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶיךָ֮ בּוֹ֒ אַתָּ֨ה וּבִנְךָ֤ וּבִתֶּ֨ךָ֙ וְעַבְדְּךָ֣ וַאֲמָתֶ֔ךָ וְהַלֵּוִ֖י אֲשֶׁ֣ר בִּשְׁעָרֶ֑יךָ וְשָׂמַחְתָּ֗ לִפְנֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ בְּכֹ֖ל מִשְׁלַ֥ח יָדֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: for rather before Yahweh your God you shall eat it in the place which will choose Yahweh your God in it, you and your son and your daughter and your male slave and your female slave and the Levite who [is] in your gates, and you shall rejoice before Yahweh your God in all [the] undertaking of your hand.
pieces: but you are to eat them in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, at the place that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will choose, you and your son and daughter, your male and female servants, and the Levite who lives in your towns. Rejoice there before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God in all that you have set your hand to.

L.18: but before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God you shall eat it, in the place that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will choose, you and your son and your daughter and your male slave and your female slave and the Levite who [is] within your gates, and you shall rejoice before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God in all the undertaking of your hand.

R.18: Instead, eat them in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, at the place that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will choose. Eat them there with your sons and daughters, your servants, and the Levites who live in your towns. Be glad there in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God for everything you have worked for.

decisions.choice: eat it: all these gifts together
decisions.reason: "It" gathers up everything listed in verse 17 as one.

decisions.choice: you and your son and your daughter ... and you shall rejoice: as in verses 7 and 12
decisions.reason: The verse repeats the joyful meal of verses 7 and 12, now addressed to each Israelite. See the notes there on slaves, "gates" and the Levite.

decisions.choice: eat them; sons and daughters; the Levites
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "them" for the gifts as a group. Readable uses plurals for son, daughter and Levite, which each stand for all of them, and "servants" as in verse 12.

records.source: הִשָּׁ֣מֶר לְךָ֔ פֶּֽן־תַּעֲזֹ֖ב אֶת־הַלֵּוִ֑י כָּל־יָמֶ֖יךָ עַל־אַדְמָתֶֽךָ׃ס
records.gloss: Take heed to yourself lest you forsake the Levite all your days on your land.
pieces: Be careful not to neglect the Levite as long as you live in your land.

L.19: Take care for yourself that you do not forsake the Levite all your days on your land.

R.19: Make sure you never fail to take care of the Levites as long as you live in your land.

decisions.choice: forsake: leave without support
decisions.reason: To forsake the Levite is to stop sharing the gifts on which he lives (14:27, 29). The verse closes the section on the sanctuary meal by naming the one most likely to be forgotten.

decisions.choice: your land: the soil of the land
decisions.reason: The word is the one in verse 1, the farmed ground. As long as Israel lives from that land, it is to support those who have none.

decisions.choice: never fail to take care of
decisions.reason: Readable says positively what "do not forsake" requires.

records.source: כִּֽי־יַרְחִיב֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֥יךָ אֶֽת־גְּבֽוּלְךָ֮ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּר־לָךְ֒ וְאָמַרְתָּ֙ אֹכְלָ֣ה בָשָׂ֔ר כִּֽי־תְאַוֶּ֥ה נַפְשְׁךָ֖ לֶאֱכֹ֣ל בָּשָׂ֑ר בְּכָל־אַוַּ֥ת נַפְשְׁךָ֖ תֹּאכַ֥ל בָּשָֽׂר׃
records.gloss: When enlarges Yahweh your God your territory, as he spoke to you, and you say, Let me eat meat, because desires your soul to eat meat, with all [the] desire of your soul you may eat meat.
pieces: When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God enlarges your territory as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised you, and you say, 'I want to eat some meat,' because you are longing for meat, you may eat meat whenever you want.

L.20: When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God enlarges your territory, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has spoken to you, and you say, 'Let me eat meat,' because your soul desires to eat meat, with all the desire of your soul you may eat meat.

R.20: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will make your land larger, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised you. Then you may say, 'I want to eat some meat,' because you are hungry for it. You may eat meat whenever you want.

decisions.choice: enlarges your territory, as he has spoken: God's promise of wide borders
decisions.reason: God promised land from the wilderness to the Euphrates (Genesis 15:18; Exodus 23:31; 11:24). As the land grows, more households will live far from the chosen place (verse 21).

decisions.choice: your soul desires: you have an appetite
decisions.reason: The "soul" is the living person with his hunger and wants. The craving is not blamed; it is simply allowed.

decisions.choice: let me eat meat: the wish of the speaker
decisions.reason: The verb form expresses a wish or resolve: "I want to eat meat".

decisions.choice: promised; you are longing / you are hungry; whenever you want
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "promised" for "spoken", which is its sense here, and put "your soul" as "you" and "the desire of your soul" as "whenever you want". Literal keeps "soul".

decisions.choice: The LORD your God will make your land larger ... Then
decisions.reason: Readable turns the long "when" sentence into three short ones.

records.heading: Eating meat in your towns

records.source: כִּֽי־יִרְחַ֨ק מִמְּךָ֜ הַמָּק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִבְחַ֜ר יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶיךָ֮ לָשׂ֣וּם שְׁמ֣וֹ שָׁם֒ וְזָבַחְתָּ֞ מִבְּקָרְךָ֣ וּמִצֹּֽאנְךָ֗ אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֤ן יְהוָה֙ לְךָ֔ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר צִוִּיתִ֑ךָ וְאָֽכַלְתָּ֙ בִּשְׁעָרֶ֔יךָ בְּכֹ֖ל אַוַּ֥ת נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃
records.gloss: If is far from you the place which will choose Yahweh your God to put his name there, then you may slaughter from your herd and from your flock which has given Yahweh to you, as I commanded you, and you may eat in your gates in all [the] desire of your soul.
pieces: If the place where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God chooses to put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name is too far from you, you may slaughter animals from the herds and flocks that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given you, as I have commanded you, and eat them in your own towns whenever you wish.

L.21: If the place that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will choose to put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name there is too far from you, then you may slaughter from your herd and from your flock that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given you, as I have commanded you, and you may eat within your gates with all the desire of your soul.

R.21: The place that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God chooses for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name may be too far away from you. If so, you may kill some of the cattle, sheep or goats that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given you, in the way I have told you. Then you may eat the meat in your own town whenever you want.

decisions.choice: if it is far from you: too far to bring every animal for slaughter
decisions.reason: The verse explains the permission of verse 15. A household far from the chosen place cannot bring each animal it wants to eat there, so it may kill it at home.

decisions.choice: as I have commanded you: in the way already laid down
alternatives: according to a rule of slaughter not recorded here
decisions.reason: The phrase most likely points to the rules just given, above all that the blood is poured out and not eaten (verse 16). It may also refer to a way of slaughter that is not written down here.

decisions.choice: may be too far away ... If so
decisions.reason: Readable splits the condition into its own sentence.

records.source: אַ֗ךְ כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יֵאָכֵ֤ל אֶֽת־הַצְּבִי֙ וְאֶת־הָ֣אַיָּ֔ל כֵּ֖ן תֹּאכְלֶ֑נּוּ הַטָּמֵא֙ וְהַטָּה֔וֹר יַחְדָּ֖ו יֹאכְלֶֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: Surely as is eaten the gazelle and the deer, so you shall eat it; the unclean and the clean alike may eat it.
pieces: Eat it just as a gazelle or a deer is eaten; those who are ritually unclean and those who are clean may eat it alike.

L.22: Indeed, as the gazelle and the deer are eaten, so you shall eat it; the unclean and the clean alike may eat it.

R.22: Eat it the way you would eat a gazelle or a deer. People who are ritually clean and people who are not may both eat it.

decisions.choice: as the gazelle and the deer; the unclean and the clean: as in verse 15
decisions.reason: The verse repeats verse 15: meat killed at home is like hunted game, not an offering, so ritual cleanness does not matter. See the note there.

decisions.choice: ritually unclean / ritually clean
decisions.reason: As in verse 15.

records.source: רַ֣ק חֲזַ֗ק לְבִלְתִּי֙ אֲכֹ֣ל הַדָּ֔ם כִּ֥י הַדָּ֖ם ה֣וּא הַנָּ֑פֶשׁ וְלֹא־תֹאכַ֥ל הַנֶּ֖פֶשׁ עִם־הַבָּשָֽׂר׃
records.gloss: Only be strong to not eat the blood, for the blood, it [is] the life, and not you shall eat the life with the meat.
pieces: Only be sure that you do not eat the blood, because the blood is the life, and you must not eat the life with the meat.

L.23: Only be firm not to eat the blood, for the blood, it [is] the life, and you shall not eat the life with the meat.

R.23: But be very careful never to eat the blood. The blood is the life, and you must not eat the life along with the meat.

decisions.choice: be strong: hold firm, do not give way
decisions.reason: The verb means to be strong or resolute. The command is pressed hard because the freedom to eat meat at home, away from the altar, makes the ban easy to forget.

decisions.choice: the life: the living soul of the animal
decisions.reason: The word is the same as "soul" in verses 15, 20 and 21, here the life of a living creature. Blood is the life because it carries it (Genesis 9:4; Leviticus 17:11, 14).

decisions.choice: you shall not eat the life: life belongs to God
decisions.reason: Meat is God's gift to eat, but the life of the creature is his alone. Pouring out the blood gives the life back to him.

pieces: Do not eat it; pour it out on the ground like water.

L.24: You shall not eat it; on the ground you shall pour it out like water.

R.24: Do not eat it. Pour it out on the ground like water.

decisions.choice: pour it out like water: as in verse 16
decisions.reason: The rule of verse 16 is repeated almost word for word, for emphasis. See the note there.

records.gloss: Not you shall eat it, so that it may go well for you and for your sons after you, for you will do the right in [the] eyes of Yahweh.
pieces: Do not eat it, so that all may go well with you and your {{gender:children|sons}} after you, because you will be doing what is right in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.25: You shall not eat it, so that it may go well with you and with your {{gender:children|sons}} after you, because you will do what [is] right in the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.25: Do not eat it. Then things will go well for you and for your {{gender:children|sons}} after you, because you will be doing what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says is right.

decisions.choice: right in the eyes of the LORD: set against what is right in one's own eyes
decisions.reason: Verse 8 spoke of each one doing what is right "in his own eyes". Here the measure is what is right in God's eyes, as also in 6:18 and 13:19.

decisions.choice: so that it may go well with you: the promise that goes with obedience
decisions.reason: The phrase recurs in Deuteronomy (4:40; 5:16; 6:3, 18). Keeping even this small rule is part of the life with God that brings his blessing to the generations that follow.

decisions.choice: your sons: your children and descendants
decisions.reason: The word is "sons", used for all of a person's children and those who come after them.

decisions.choice: {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: The default "children" says that daughters are included; the setting gives the traditional "sons".

records.source: רַ֧ק קָֽדָשֶׁ֛יךָ אֲשֶׁר־יִהְי֥וּ לְךָ֖ וּנְדָרֶ֑יךָ תִּשָּׂ֣א וּבָ֔אתָ אֶל־הַמָּק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁר־יִבְחַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Only your holy things which will be to you and your vows you shall carry and you shall come to the place which will choose Yahweh.
pieces: But take your holy offerings that are due from you and your vow offerings, and go with them to the place that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will choose.

L.26: Only your holy things that you have and your vow offerings you shall take up, and you shall come to the place that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will choose.

R.26: But take the holy gifts you owe and the gifts you promised, and go with them to the place that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will choose.

decisions.choice: your holy things that are yours: what you have set apart for God
alternatives: the holy things that you have
decisions.reason: "Holy things" are gifts that belong to God, such as tithes and firstborn animals (verse 17). "Which will be to you" may mean the holy gifts that fall due from you, or simply those you have. Either way they are not ordinary meat.

decisions.choice: only: holy gifts keep the old rule
decisions.reason: After the freedom of verses 20-25, "only" marks the limit: what is holy must still be brought to the chosen place.

decisions.choice: that are due from you / you owe
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable take "which will be to you" as the gifts that fall due. Literal keeps "that you have", which leaves the phrase open.

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ עֹלֹתֶ֨יךָ֙ הַבָּשָׂ֣ר וְהַדָּ֔ם עַל־מִזְבַּ֖ח יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ וְדַם־זְבָחֶ֗יךָ יִשָּׁפֵךְ֙ עַל־מִזְבַּח֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ וְהַבָּשָׂ֖ר תֹּאכֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And you shall make your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood, on [the] altar of Yahweh your God, and [the] blood of your sacrifices shall be poured out on [the] altar of Yahweh your God, and the flesh you shall eat.
pieces: Offer your burnt offerings, both meat and blood, on the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. The blood of your other sacrifices is to be poured out on the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, but you may eat the meat.

L.27: And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the meat and the blood, on the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God; and the blood of your sacrifices shall be poured out on the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and the meat you shall eat.

R.27: Offer your burnt offerings on the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, with their meat and their blood. For your other sacrifices, pour the blood out on the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, but you may eat the meat.

decisions.choice: burnt offerings, the meat and the blood: the whole animal is given
decisions.reason: In a burnt offering all the meat was burned on the altar and the blood was splashed against it (Leviticus 1:5-9); the worshiper kept nothing.

decisions.choice: the blood of your sacrifices poured out; the meat eaten
decisions.reason: In a sacrifice for a meal, the blood went to the altar and the fat was burned, and the worshipers ate the meat (Leviticus 3:1-5; 7:15-16). That is the joyful meal of verses 7 and 18.

decisions.choice: on the altar: on it or against its side
decisions.reason: The preposition can mean "on" or "beside". The blood was splashed against the altar or poured out at its base (Leviticus 1:5; 4:7), so it went to the altar, not on the fire.

decisions.choice: your other sacrifices
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "other" to show that burnt offerings are sacrifices too, but this rule is for the ones that are eaten.

records.gloss: Keep and hear all the words the these which I [am] commanding you, so that it may go well for you and for your sons after you until forever, for you will do the good and the right in [the] eyes of Yahweh your God.
pieces: Be careful to obey all these words I am commanding you, so that all may go well with you and your {{gender:children|sons}} after you forever, because you will be doing what is good and right in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

L.28: Keep and listen to all these words that I am commanding you, so that it may go well with you and with your {{gender:children|sons}} after you forever, because you will do what [is] good and right in the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

R.28: Be careful to obey everything I am telling you. Then things will always go well for you and your {{gender:children|sons}} after you, because you will be doing what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God says is good and right.

decisions.choice: keep and hear: listen and carefully obey
decisions.reason: "Hear" in Deuteronomy means to listen so as to obey (6:3-4), and "keep" means to guard and do. Together they call for careful obedience.

decisions.choice: the good and the right in the eyes of the LORD: as in 6:18
decisions.reason: The verse sums up the chapter in the words of verse 25 and 6:18, adding "good" and "forever".

decisions.choice: be careful to obey
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable join the two verbs into one plain command. Literal keeps both.

decisions.choice: {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: As in verse 25.

records.source: כִּֽי־יַכְרִית֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ אֶת־הַגּוֹיִ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר אַתָּ֥ה בָא־שָׁ֛מָּה לָרֶ֥שֶׁת אוֹתָ֖ם מִפָּנֶ֑יךָ וְיָרַשְׁתָּ֣ אֹתָ֔ם וְיָשַׁבְתָּ֖ בְּאַרְצָֽם׃
records.gloss: When cuts off Yahweh your God the nations where you [are] going there to dispossess them from before you, and you dispossess them and you live in their land,
pieces: When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God cuts off before you the nations you are going in to drive out, and you drive them out and settle in their land,

L.29: When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God cuts off from before you the nations whom you are going in to dispossess, and you dispossess them and live in their land,

R.29: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will destroy the nations in the land you are going into. You will drive them out and live in their land.

decisions.choice: cuts off: destroys, removes
decisions.reason: To "cut off" a people is to destroy it or remove it from the land. God is the one who does it (7:1-2; 19:1).

decisions.choice: where you are going in to dispossess them: the land you are entering
decisions.reason: The phrase means the nations in the land Israel is about to enter and take. "Dispossess" is used twice: God's act makes Israel's possible.

decisions.choice: drive out
decisions.reason: As in verse 2: "dispossess" at Literal, "drive out" at Balanced and Readable. Readable turns the opening "when" into a statement of what will happen; verse 30 then begins "When that happens".

records.heading: Do not follow the ways of the nations

records.source: הִשָּׁ֣מֶר לְךָ֗ פֶּן־תִּנָּקֵשׁ֙ אַחֲרֵיהֶ֔ם אַחֲרֵ֖י הִשָּׁמְדָ֣ם מִפָּנֶ֑יךָ וּפֶן־תִּדְרֹ֨שׁ לֵֽאלֹהֵיהֶ֜ם לֵאמֹ֨ר אֵיכָ֨ה יַעַבְד֜וּ הַגּוֹיִ֤ם הָאֵ֨לֶּה֙ אֶת־אֱלֹ֣הֵיהֶ֔ם וְאֶעֱשֶׂה־כֵּ֖ן גַּם־אָֽנִי׃
records.gloss: take heed to yourself lest you be ensnared after them, after their being destroyed from before you, and lest you inquire about their gods, saying, How did serve the nations the these their gods? And I will do so, also I.
pieces: be careful not to be trapped into following them after they have been destroyed before you. Do not ask about their gods, saying, 'How did these nations worship their gods? I will do the same.'

L.30: take care for yourself that you are not ensnared [to follow] after them, after they have been destroyed before you, and that you do not inquire about their gods, saying, 'How did these nations serve their gods? And I also will do so.'

R.30: When that happens, be careful! Even after they are destroyed, do not be trapped into doing what they did. Do not ask about their gods and say, 'How did these nations worship their gods? I want to do the same.'

decisions.choice: ensnared after them: lured into following their ways
decisions.reason: A snare is a bird trap. The danger is not the nations' armies, which God will destroy, but their worship, which can catch Israel like a bird in a trap (7:16, 25).

decisions.choice: inquire about their gods: seek them out in order to copy them
decisions.reason: It is the verb "seek" of verse 5. Israel is to seek the place God chooses, not to seek out how the nations worshiped their gods.

decisions.choice: I also will do so: the wish to worship the LORD in the nations' way
decisions.reason: The speaker does not plan to leave the LORD, but to copy the nations' rites in worshiping him. Verse 31 forbids exactly that.

decisions.choice: worship
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "worship" for "serve", as in verse 2.

decisions.choice: When that happens
decisions.reason: Readable begins a new sentence here and links it to verse 29.

records.source: לֹא־תַעֲשֶׂ֣ה כֵ֔ן לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ כִּי֩ כָּל־תּוֹעֲבַ֨ת יְהוָ֜ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׂנֵ֗א עָשׂוּ֙ לֵאלֹ֣הֵיהֶ֔ם כִּ֣י גַ֤ם אֶת־בְּנֵיהֶם֙ וְאֶת־בְּנֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם יִשְׂרְפ֥וּ בָאֵ֖שׁ לֵֽאלֹהֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Not you shall do so to Yahweh your God, for every abomination of Yahweh which he hates they have done for their gods, for even their sons and their daughters they burn in the fire to their gods.
pieces: You must not worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God in that way, because for their gods they have done every detestable thing that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} hates. They even burn their sons and daughters in the fire as offerings to their gods.

L.31: You shall not do so to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, for every abomination to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} hates, they have done for their gods; for they even burn their sons and their daughters in the fire to their gods.

R.31: Do not worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God the way they worship their gods. When they worship their gods, they do all the disgusting things that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} hates. They even burn their own sons and daughters as sacrifices to their gods.

decisions.choice: you shall not do so: as in verse 4
decisions.reason: The chapter returns to the words of verse 4. There they forbade worship at the nations' places; here they forbid the nations' ways of worship.

decisions.choice: abomination: something God finds utterly detestable
decisions.reason: The word names what is loathsome and rejected, here what the LORD hates. Deuteronomy uses it of idols (7:25-26) and of the practices of the nations (18:9-12).

decisions.choice: they burn their sons and daughters: child sacrifice
decisions.reason: Some peoples of the region offered children by burning them. The law forbids it outright (18:10; Leviticus 18:21), and the prophets condemn it when it later appears in Israel (2 Kings 16:3; Jeremiah 7:31).

decisions.choice: as offerings / as sacrifices
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the burning was: an offering to their gods, which "to their gods" means.
